algangror_1.m: Oh my, a child. He he, how nice. Tell me, what brings you here?
r: I am looking for my brother.
I just entered to see if there's any loot to be found here.
I'm an adventurer, looking to help anyone in need of help.
I am sent by Jhaeld to end whatever it is you do to the people of Remgard.

algangror_2a.m: Run away, has he? He he.

algangror_2b.m: Oh sure, you think you can just pick up anything and claim it as yours?

algangror_2c.m: How noble. Maybe you can be of use to me.

algangror_3.m: Tell me, now that you have entered this house, would you be willing to help me with a small ... problem?
r: Maybe, it depends on what the problem is.
Maybe, it depends on what type of reward we are talking about.
No way. You are acting way too creepy for me.

algangror_3c.m: Reward? No, no, I don't have anything to give you, unfortunately.
r: I guess you won't get any help either then.
Fine, what's the problem you want help with?
Something feels wrong here. I better not get involved in this.

algangror_4.m: You see, I have this slight problem with ... ahem ... vermin.

algangror_5.m: Always sneaking around, always trying to cause mischief.

algangror_6.m: Fortunately, I managed to capture some of them, and locked them in my basement.

algangror_7.m: Now, I can't handle them myself because of certain ... issues.

algangror_8.m: That's where you come in. Would you be willing to ... ahem ... handle those rodents for me?
r: Sure, some rodents, I can handle that.
No problem, I'll be right back once I have killed them.
Something feels wrong here. I better not get involved in this.

algangror_9.m: Splendid. Return to me with some proof that they have been dealt with.

algangror_cmp1.m: So, for helping me with the idols, I believe I promised you my enchanted necklace, 'Marrowtaint'.

algangror_cmp2.m: Wear it well, my friend. Do not let others get hold of the power that Marrowtaint provides.

r: That's all? One lousy necklace for all this trouble I went through?

algangror_cmp4.m: Do not underestimate it, my friend.

algangror_cmp5.m: Again, thank you for helping me. You will always be welcome here, friend.

algangror_decline_1.m: Ah yes. After all, you are just a child and I can understand such a task would be too much for you. He he.

algangror_fight_3.m: Jhaeld, the fool. He hides behind his guards and his stone walls. Such a pitiful man he is. Yes, I made those people disappear, but they were all worth it. I will have my revenge!

algangror_fight_4.m: And you, what are you trying to accomplish by running his errands? How fortunate that you entered my house. He he.

algangror_fight_5.m: Do you really think you can defeat *me*? Ha ha, this will be fun!

algangror_remgard_1.m: Oh, it's not far from here. Doesn't matter really.

algangror_remgard_2.m: You see, I used to live there. To make a long story short, there were some ... ahem ... misunderstandings.

algangror_remgard_3.m: These days, I think they are looking for me, for some reason. Can't think of any reason why really. But I believe they are.

algangror_remgard_4.m: Because of our previous ... misunderstanding, I think it's best they don't find out that I'm here.

algangror_remgard_5.m: Therefore, I ask of you not to reveal my whereabouts to them.

algangror_remgard_6.m: Thank you. Under no circumstances should you tell them where I am. They will most likely try to persuade you into revealing my location.

algangror_return_1.m: You return. Did you handle all those ... ahem ... rodents in my basement?
r: I am still working on it. Goodbye.
I won't do your stupid task, count me out.
I have decided not to help you with your rodents.
I am sent by Jhaeld to end whatever it is you do to the people of Remgard.

algangror_return_2.m: He he. I bet you sure showed them. Excellent. Thank you for ... ahem ... helping me.

algangror_return_3.m: Those rodents have really been bothering me. Good thing I managed to catch some of them. He he.

algangror_return_4.m: Now, there was something else I wanted to talk to you about. Have you been to the city of Remgard in your travels?

algangror_return_c1.m: You return. Thank you for helping me with my ... ahem ... rodent problem earlier.

algangror_return_c3.m: I hope that will teach those *other* rats.

algangror_return_c4.m: Say, you seem like a resourceful person. Would you be interested in helping me with yet another ... task?

algangror_return_d2.m: You should probably leave before you tip something over that might ... ahem ... break. He he.
r: I was sent by Jhaeld to end whatever it is you are doing to the people of Remgard.
You are right, I had better leave.

algangror_story.m: Let me tell you my story.
r: Can we just skip to the end?

algangror_story1.m: You see, I used to live in the city of Remgard. The times were good, and the city prospered.

algangror_story10.m: So I told myself that others would not hinder me in my curiosity to better myself.

algangror_story11.m: Those books that I bought from the Blackmarrow residence in Nor City - I must have read them all perhaps five times over. This was something completely new to me, and at the same time very exciting.

algangror_story12.m: For some reason, the others in Remgard started giving me strange looks, and I could hear the whispers behind my back.

algangror_story13.m: I was even barred from the tavern. 'People come here for a good time, and we don't want people like you here ruining that' they said. What fools they are.

algangror_story14.m: I heard one woman whispering to her boy, 'Don't look at her, she'll turn you to stone!'. Others just turned the other way when they met me.

algangror_story16.m: One day, Jhaeld showed up at my doorstep with a group of guards.

algangror_story17.m: The people of Remgard had decided that I could not stay there anymore, he said. The things I did were causing other people harm, he said.

algangror_story18.m: What had I done, I asked myself? I had never hurt anyone, much less affected anyone with my ... experiments. Am I not allowed to do what I wish?

algangror_story19.m: I had little chance to argue, however. The guards led me out of the city. They did not even let me gather my things. All my books, all my notes and all my findings - gone. I lost everything.

algangror_story2.m: Our crops grew well, and some people had very fortunate trading agreements with other cities, making the life for most of us living in Remgard very easy.

algangror_story20.m: All this happened several seasons ago. I knew I had to get revenge for what they did to me.

algangror_story21.m: Oh, how I despise them all. The people that gave me those looks, the people that whispered behind my back, and most of all that fool Jhaeld.

algangror_story22.m: So, I decided to extend my ... experiments ... to larger things. To people, to living things. This is the perfect opportunity to learn even more than what is in the books.

algangror_story23.m: To think that I could do it while at the same time get revenge on those despicable people - it's an excellent plan, if I may say so myself. He he.
r: So, what happened to all those people that have gone missing?

algangror_story24.m: I lured them here. Once I managed to trap them, I placed a curse on them that, in theory, should have only made them unable to speak.

algangror_story25.m: Maybe I haven't understood everything correctly from the books that I have read, since instead of making them unable to speak, they were all turned into rats instead.

algangror_story26.m: Practice makes perfect, I suppose. Ha ha.
r: Wait, does this mean that those rats I killed for you were...

algangror_story27.m: Oh yes. With your help, they are now one less problem to deal with, so to speak. He he.

algangror_story28.m: So, that's my story. Thank you for listening to it.
r: I understand, and I agree with your actions.
I do not fully agree with your actions.
What you did could never be justified!

algangror_story29a.m: Thank you. It is good to know there are more people interested in learning more.

algangror_story29b.m: I never expected you to understand it. No one else seems to understand me either. Oh well, your loss, I guess.

algangror_story3.m: I even sold some of the baskets that I used to make to a wealthy merchant that visited us from Nor City.

algangror_story4.m: However, even the easy life gets boring after a while. I believe it is in our nature to strive for new and better things, to free us from the boredom of day-to-day life.

algangror_story5.m: I wanted to learn more of things that I knew nothing about, and wanted to explore things I had only read of in books before.

algangror_story6.m: So I went to Nor City myself, and visited many ... interesting people and ... dark corners.

algangror_story7.m: Naturally, I was thrilled of the knowledge I gained from the experience, and from what I learned while there.

algangror_story8.m: As I got back home, I wanted to continue practicing what I had observed and learned while in Nor City.

algangror_story9.m: You could say I got obsessed with learning more. I guess the others living in Remgard did not ... share my enthusiasm. Some of them even questioned the fact that I wanted to learn more.

algangror_task2_1.m: Now, I can't tell you what task I have in mind before I am confident that you will actually help me. Granted, you have already shown some level of respect for my need of discretion.

algangror_task2_10.m: Remember, it is of utmost importance that you be as discreet as possible about this. The idols must not be found once you have placed them, and no one must notice that you place the idols.

algangror_task2_11.m: So, the first person that I want you to visit is Jhaeld. I hear that he spends most of his time in the Remgard tavern these days.

algangror_task2_12.m: Secondly, I want you to visit one of the farmers named Larni. He lives with his wife Caeda here in Remgard in one of the northern cabins.

algangror_task2_13.m: The third person is Arnal the weapon-smith, that lives in the northwest of Remgard.

algangror_task2_14.m: Fourth is Emerei, that can probably be found in his house to the southeast of Remgard.

algangror_task2_15.m: The fifth person is the farmer Carthe. Carthe lives on the eastern shore of Remgard, near the tavern.

algangror_task2_16.m: Once you have placed these five idols by the beds of these five people, return to me as soon as possible.

algangror_task2_17.m: Again, I cannot stress this enough - you must not tell anyone about these idols, and you must not be seen while placing them.

algangror_task2_19.m: Now go, and please hurry, we might not have much time.

algangror_task2_2.m: Nor can I describe my reasoning behind this task before you are done with it.

algangror_task2_3.m: Rest assured, you will be sufficiently rewarded by helping me. In fact, you see this necklace here? It has some peculiar powers that many people seek.

algangror_task2_4.m: The world around you seems to move a bit slower when you wear it.
r: OK. I will help you with your task.
OK, I'll help. I'm always interested in new items.
It all depends on what you want me to do.
Something feels wrong here. I don't think I should help you.

algangror_task2_5.m: As I said, I cannot tell you what task I have in mind, or my reasoning behind it until you are done. I would need your total ... cooperation with this.
r: OK. I will agree to help you with your task.
OK, I'll help. I'm always interested in new items.
No. I will not help you unless you tell me what you want me to do.
No, I would never help someone like you.

algangror_task2_7.m: You will tell no one of this task that I am about to give you, and you must be as discreet as possible.

algangror_task2_8.m: I have in my possession five idols. Five idols with very unique ... qualities. What I want you to do is ... deliver these idols to various people in the town of Remgard.

algangror_task2_9.m: You will place them by the beds of five particular persons, and you must hide it well so that the person does not find the idol itself.

algangror_task2_d.m: Very well, return to me once you are ready.

algangror_task2_done1.m: Excellent. Maybe, now I can rest easily. Thank you so much for helping me.

algangror_task2_done2.m: Did anyone see you or where you placed the idols?
r: No, I hid the idols as you instructed.

algangror_task2_done3.m: Good. Thank you again for helping me.

algangror_task2_n.m: Ah yes. After all, you are just a child and I can understand that all of this must be too much for you. Hee hee.

algangror_task2_n2.m: Can I at least urge you not to disclose my location to the people of Remgard?
r: I will keep your location secret. Goodbye.
Don't tell me what to do! Goodbye.

algangror_task2_ret1.m: Tell me, how goes the task of placing the idols?
r: Can you repeat what you wanted me to do?
I am still trying to find everyone.
I won't do your stupid task.
I will not help you with your task.

algangror_task2_ret2.m: Please hurry, we might not have much time.

algangror_told_2.m: Say, despite my previous urging to you to keep my location a secret to the people of Remgard, I have this feeling that this trust has been broken. Please tell me it isn't so.
r: Yes, I have told Jhaeld where you are.
[Lie] No, I have not told anyone.

algangror_told_3.m: I can feel it in me.

remgard2.10: I have told Jhaeld, the village elder in Remgard, about the woman named Algangror that lives in the abandoned house to the east along the northern shore of the lake outside Remgard.
remgard2.20: Jhaeld told me that he would rather not deal with her, since he believes she is very dangerous. For the sake of his guards, he will not risk going against her since he is afraid of what might happen to all of them.
remgard2.21: If I want to help Jhaeld and the people of Remgard, I should find a way to make Algangror disappear. He also warns me to be extremely careful.
remgard2.30: Algangror admitted to me that she had made some people disappear from Remgard. She would not tell me what happened to them though.
remgard2.35: I have started attacking Algangror. I should return to Jhaeld with proof of defeating her when she is dead.
remgard2.40: I have told Jhaeld that I defeated Algangror.
remgard2.41: Jhaeld was very pleased to hear the good news. The people of Remgard should now be safe, and the town can be opened to outsiders again.
remgard2.45: For helping the people of Remgard find the cause of the disappearing people, Jhaeld told me to talk to Rothses. He might be able to improve some of my equipment.
remgard2.46: Ervelyn, the Remgard tailor, gave me a feathered hat as thanks for helping the people of Remgard find out what happened to the missing people.

remgard.10: I have reached the bridge to enter the town of Remgard. According to the bridge guard, the town is closed for outsiders to enter, and no-one is currently allowed to leave. They are investigating some disappearances of some of the townspeople.
remgard.15: I have offered my assistance in helping the people of Remgard investigate what has happened to the townspeople that have disappeared.
remgard.20: The bridge guard has asked me to investigate an abandoned house to the east along the northern shore of the lake. I should be wary of any inhabitants that may be there.
remgard.30: I have reported back to the bridge guard that I met Algangror in the abandoned house.
remgard.31: I have reported back to the bridge guard that the abandoned house was empty.
remgard.35: I have been granted entrance into Remgard. I should go visit Jhaeld, the town elder, to talk about what the next step should be. Jhaeld can probably be found in the tavern to the southeast.
remgard.40: Jhaeld was rather arrogant, but told me that they have had a problem with people disappearing for a while now. They have no clue what could be causing it.
remgard.50: I should visit four people in Remgard, and ask them about any clues on what might have happened to the missing people.
remgard.51: First is Norath, whose wife Bethir has disappeared. Norath can be found in the south-westernmost farmhouse.
remgard.52: Second, I should go talk to the Knights of Elythom, here in the tavern.
remgard.53: Third, I should go talk to the old woman Duaina in her house to the south.
remgard.54: Lastly, I should talk to Rothses, the armorer. He lives on the west side of town.
remgard.59: I tried to tell Jhaeld about Algangror, but he dismissed me as he had not heard me.
remgard.61: I have talked to Norath. He and his wife had been fighting recently, but he has no idea on what may have happened to her.
remgard.62: The Knights of Elythom in the Remgard tavern have had one of their knights disappearing recently. No one noticed anything when she disappeared, however.
remgard.63: Duaina has seen me in her visions. I did not understand all that she spoke of, but the parts that were clear were that me and Andor were parts of a larger plot. I wonder what this means? She did not speak of any disappearing people however, not that I could understand anyway.
remgard.64: Rothses told me that Bethir visited him the night before she disappeared, to sell some equipment. He did not see where she went after that.
remgard.70: I have talked to all of the people that Jhaeld wanted me to talk to, but did not get any information from any of them about what may have happened to the missing people. I should go back to Jhaeld and ask what his plans are next.
remgard.75: Jhaeld was really upset that I did not find out anything from the people that I was sent to talk to.
remgard.80: If I still want to help Jhaeld and the people of Remgard, I should look for clues in other places.
remgard.110: Jhaeld does not want to talk to me. I will not help them find out what happened to the missing people of Remgard.

fiveidols.10: Algangror wants me to help her with a task. She cannot describe the nature of the task, or the reasoning behind it. If I help her, she has promised to give me her enchanted necklace, that apparently is worth a lot.
fiveidols.20: I have agreed to help Algangror with her task.
fiveidols.30: Algangror wants me to place five idols near five different people in Remgard. The idols should be placed near the beds of these five people, and must be hidden so that they are not found easily.
fiveidols.31: The first person is Jhaeld, the village elder that can be found in the Remgard tavern.
fiveidols.32: Second, I should place an idol by the bed of Larni the farmer, that lives in one of the northern cabins in Remgard.
fiveidols.33: The third person is Arnal the weapon-smith, that lives in the northwest of Remgard.
fiveidols.34: Fourth is Emerei, that can be found to the southeast of Remgard.
fiveidols.35: The fifth person is Carthe. Carthe lives on the eastern shore of Remgard, near the tavern.
fiveidols.37: I must not tell anyone of my task, or of the placement of the idols.
fiveidols.41: I have placed an idol by Jhaeld's bed.
fiveidols.42: I have placed an idol by Larni the farmer's bed.
fiveidols.43: I have placed an idol by Arnal's bed.
fiveidols.44: I have placed an idol by Emerei's bed.
fiveidols.45: I have placed an idol by Carthe's bed.
fiveidols.50: All the idols have been placed by the beds of the people that Algangror told me to visit. I should return to Algangror.
fiveidols.51: Algangror thanked me for helping her.
fiveidols.60: She told me her story, with how she used to live in the city, but was persecuted for her beliefs. According to her, the persecution was totally unjustified since she does no harm to people.
fiveidols.61: To take revenge on the city of Remgard, she managed to lure some people into her cabin and turn them into rats.
fiveidols.70: For helping her with the tasks that she could not perform herself, Algangror gave me her enchanted necklace, 'Marrowtaint'.
fiveidols.100: I have decided not to help Algangror with her task.

algangror.10: In a lonely house on a peninsula at the northern shore of lake Laeroth up in the mountains to the north-east, I met a woman called Algangror.
algangror.11: She has a rodent problem and needs help dealing with some of them that she has trapped in her basement.
algangror.15: I have agreed to help Algangror deal with her rodent problem. I should return to her when I have killed all six rodents in her basement.
algangror.20: Algangror thanked me for helping her with her problem.
algangror.21: She also told me not to talk to anyone in Remgard about her whereabouts. Apparently, they are looking for her for some reason that she would not say. Under no circumstances should I tell anyone where she is.
algangror.100: I will not help Algangror with her task.
algangror.101: Algangror won't talk to me, and I will be unable to help her with her task.

sk.fightstyleUnarmedUnarmored: Fighting style: Way of the monk
